clue.text: Broken car phone in Escort

indicators.note: something broken has its parts out of their proper order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A smashed mobile phone found inside a Ford Escort car.
explanation.walkthrough: Escort looks like the Ford car model, which suits the car phone, but it is the definition: a chaperon escorts a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies and supervises someone, typically a young unmarried woman, at social occasions.

clue.text: Risk not completing part of the church

indicators.note: not completing means stopping short, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar, for clergy and choir

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gamble by leaving a section of a church unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name a possibility of something happening, often an unwelcome one, as in taking a gamble.

clue.text: A king can't recollect trigonometrical function

indicators.note: read as re-collect, the letters are gathered up again in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king
the word without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A monarch is unable to remember a function from his maths lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Recollect looks like remember, which suits a forgetful king, but it means collect again, rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctan is short for arc tangent, the inverse of the tangent function in trigonometry.

clue.text: It may be said to be highly complimentary

definitions.text: It may be said to be highly complimentary

blocks.note: setter's reading: it is a speech, something spoken aloud at a funeral
the speech is full of high praise for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: It may be said looks like a hedge; it literally describes a speech that is delivered, full of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing praising someone highly, especially one who has just died.

clue.text: Rare biblical book required to make up a set, perhaps

definitions.note: singular phrase for a plural answer: the numbers together form one set

blocks.note: something rare or unusual is odd
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An uncommon book of the Bible is needed to complete a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd and set suggest a missing piece to complete a collection; really the answer is a mathematical set.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers not divisible by two form an infinite set in mathematics, an example of the term.

clue.text: Thief's unusual charm

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the word with its possessive s, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A burglar carries an odd lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an object believed to hold magical power, much like an amulet or talisman worn for protection.

clue.text: Organising Sue's opal wedding

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new order, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the words letter for letter, possessive s included

explanation.walkthrough: An opal wedding looks like an anniversary; wedding alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal is a formal word for marriage or a marriage ceremony, from the verb espouse, to marry.

clue.text: Begin to explain what I did at the restaurant

blocks.note: being at a place is being in it
the restaurant is referred to by the pronoun it
taken as written
what one did at a restaurant is eat; the past tense

explanation.surface: Starting to describe one's meal at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a sentence describing a meal out: where I was, then what I did there, run together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to start or set something going, such as a process or conversation.

clue.text: Top rise forecast for seamen

blocks.note: surface reading: the best pay increase, perhaps a wage rise
setter's reading: the highest level the sea reaches, predicted in tables for sailors

explanation.walkthrough: Rise looks like a pay rise for sailors; it is the sea rising to its peak twice a day.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's peak level in its twice-daily cycle is predicted in published tables used by mariners.

clue.text: Touching display of regal appreciation

blocks.note: surface reading: a moving, emotional show of royal gratitude
setter's reading: the monarch literally touches a new knight's shoulder with a sword as an honour

explanation.walkthrough: Touching reads as moving, but here it is literal: the sword tap on the shoulder when a knighthood is conferred.
explanation.definitionFit: The original sense of the word is the ceremonial embrace or sword touch conferring knighthood, hence any award or praise.

clue.text: Season well

blocks.note: first meaning: the time of year between winter and summer
second meaning: a natural source where water rises from the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest adding salt properly; apart they are two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the time of year after winter and a source of water rising from underground.

clue.text: Result of strikes in the metal industry

definitions.text: Result of strikes in the metal industry

blocks.note: surface reading: the effect of walkouts by workers, industrial action
setter's reading: hammer blows on metal produce a loud ringing din

explanation.walkthrough: Strikes looks like trade-union action, as industry encourages; really they are blows of a hammer on metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is a continuous loud ringing noise, the kind produced by striking metal objects repeatedly.

clue.text: Fiction project about Shakespearean heroine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: to jut is to project or stick out
a lie is a fiction, an untruth

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a heroine from Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiction and project both look like nouns about a literary work; one is a falsehood, the other the verb to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet is the young lover in Romeo and Juliet, one of the best-known female leads in Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: One growing up in a cave

definitions.text: One growing up in a cave

blocks.note: surface reading: a child raised in a cave, like a caveman
setter's reading: a mineral deposit that grows upward from the cave floor

explanation.walkthrough: Growing up suggests a child; it is literal, rising from the floor, unlike its partner that hangs from the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripping mineral water builds a column of calcium carbonate upward from the floor of a cavern.

clue.text: Summarised and withdrawn

blocks.note: first meaning: reduced to a short summary, as a paper's abstract
second meaning: preoccupied, lost in thought, absent-minded

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both condensed into a brief summary and mentally absent, distracted from one's surroundings.

clue.text: Where prompt action is requested

blocks.note: surface reading: quick, immediate action
setter's reading: the prompter feeds forgotten lines to actors from the wings

explanation.walkthrough: Prompt looks like quick; it is the theatre prompter, who works out of the audience's view in the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means out of sight of the audience, in the wings where the prompter stands during a play.

clue.text: Inferior tufts of horsehair

blocks.note: surface reading: poor quality; setter's reading: lower, as in anatomy
the tufts grow low on a horse's leg, behind the joint above the hoof

explanation.walkthrough: Inferior looks like shoddy; in anatomy it means lower down, here low on the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the tufts of hair on the back of a horse's leg just above the hoof, and the joints they cover.

clue.text: The culprit's proposal about the outcome

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: an offer is a proposal
the end is the outcome or result

explanation.surface: The guilty party makes a suggestion regarding the result.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as possessive but stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is a person who has committed a crime or wrong, someone to blame.

clue.text: A fight, but nobody is charged

blocks.note: first meaning: a brawl in which everyone joins in
second meaning: read literally, admission costs nothing for anyone

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out but the police make no arrests.
explanation.walkthrough: Charged suggests the police after a fight; the setter means asked to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a chaotic brawl that anyone may join, and literally means open to everyone without payment.

clue.text: Extra large flag featuring Egyptian god

blocks.note: OS, for outsize, is the clothing label for extra large
a flag is a kind of iris, the yellow flag of riverbanks

explanation.surface: A huge banner bearing the image of an Egyptian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a banner; it is the plant, a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the ancient Egyptian god of the dead and the underworld, husband of Isis.

clue.text: Open bottle before the game, get drunk

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; get drunk frames it as becoming so

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its start, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: Uncork a bottle before the match and get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Open looks like an instruction to uncork; it picks the opening letter. Blotto is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal slang for extremely intoxicated, too drunk to function.

clue.text: One habitually taking things did wrong in law

indicators.note: something gone wrong is not in its proper order, so the letters are rearranged
in places one set of letters inside the other

blocks.note: an act is a law passed by parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A habitual thief was found to have broken the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking things suggests stealing; it means taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is a person dependent on a substance, regularly using drugs or alcohol.

clue.text: A fighting man, I go to join up

indicators.note: telling a letter to go means it is to leave, so it is taken out

blocks.note: a soldier is a man who fights in an army
taken as written; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A soldier announces he is going off to enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: Join up looks like enlisting, which fits the fighting man; here it means fusing metal parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldering fuses metal parts together with a melted alloy, a way of joining pieces such as wires.

clue.text: Encourages a boy to have a light meal

blocks.note: to egg on is to encourage, so encourages gives this
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone urges a young man to eat something light.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of chopped boiled eggs with mayonnaise or leaves is a typical simple snack or lunch.

clue.text: Agree to take the throne

blocks.note: first meaning: to consent to a request or demand
second meaning: to succeed as monarch

explanation.surface: Someone consents to become the new monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to consent to a proposal and to succeed to an office, especially becoming king or queen.

clue.text: Books for the opera

blocks.note: surface reading: volumes one might reserve or read
setter's reading: the written words of an opera, called its book

explanation.walkthrough: Books for the opera sounds like booking seats; it is the text sung, which theatre people call the book. The Italian plural ends in i.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written text of an opera or musical, and the Italian plural is used for several of them.

clue.text: Possibly run and see to make certain

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps go quickly and look, just to check.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to guarantee or secure an outcome, making sure something will happen.

clue.text: Presumably he was prepared for his main tasks

definitions.text: Presumably he was prepared for his main tasks

blocks.note: setter's reading: Be Prepared is the motto of the Scout movement
the main is the sea, so his tasks are on the water

explanation.walkthrough: Main looks like chief; in crosswords and poetry the main is the open sea. Sea scouts are a branch of the Scouts that does sailing and boating.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Scouts' water-based section lives by the motto Be Prepared, and does his tasks afloat.
